panels.head: How the pieces stack up
panels.side: a request travels top to bottom
panels.caption: Everything sits inside a project, and projects sit under folders and an organisation. A request hits the edge, is balanced, runs on compute, and reads state from the data tier.

panels.head: Compute — where code runs
panels.caption: Google's ladder is unusually clean: a VM, a Kubernetes cluster, a container that scales to zero, or a single function.

items.label: Compute Engine
items.note: Virtual machines. Per-second billing and automatic sustained-use discounts.
Managed Kubernetes from the company that wrote Kubernetes.

items.label: Cloud Run
items.note: Runs any container, scales to zero, billed per request.

items.label: Cloud Functions
items.note: A single function triggered by an event. Google's smallest compute unit.

items.label: App Engine
items.note: The original platform-as-a-service. Deploy code, ignore the machine.

items.label: Artifact Registry
items.note: Private store for container images and language packages.

panels.head: Storage — where bytes sit
panels.caption: One object store with four price tiers, plus disks for VMs and a shared file system when you need POSIX.

items.note: Object storage. Standard, Nearline, Coldline and Archive tiers by access frequency.

items.label: Persistent Disk
items.note: Block storage attached to a VM. Survives the instance being deleted.

items.label: Filestore
items.note: Managed NFS file share for machines that need a real file system.

panels.head: Databases and analytics
panels.caption: Spanner and BigQuery are the two most distinctive things Google Cloud sells — neither has a true equivalent elsewhere.

items.label: Cloud SQL
items.note: Managed MySQL, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. The default relational choice.
Relational, globally distributed, and strongly consistent at the same time.

items.label: Firestore
items.note: Document database that syncs to mobile and web clients in real time.

items.label: Bigtable
items.note: Wide-column store for very high write throughput. Powers Search and Maps.

items.label: Memorystore
items.note: Managed Redis or Memcached in front of a database.

items.label: BigQuery
items.note: Serverless warehouse. Query terabytes with SQL, priced per byte scanned.

panels.head: Networking and delivery
panels.caption: A VPC in Google Cloud is global rather than regional, which is the single biggest difference from AWS and Azure.

items.note: Your private network. Unusually, one VPC spans every region at once.

items.label: Cloud Load Balancing
items.note: One global anycast IP in front of backends in many regions.

items.label: Cloud CDN
items.note: Caches responses at Google's edge, on the same load balancer.

items.label: Cloud DNS
items.note: Hosts your DNS records on Google's anycast name servers.

items.label: Cloud Armor
items.note: WAF and DDoS protection attached to the load balancer.

items.label: Cloud NAT
items.note: Lets private instances reach the internet without a public IP.

items.label: Dedicated Interconnect
items.note: A private physical link into Google's network.

items.label: Cloud Endpoints
items.note: Manages, secures and monitors your own APIs.

panels.head: Identity and security
panels.caption: IAM binds a principal to a role on a resource. Everything else narrows what a compromised principal can reach.

items.note: Who has which role on which resource. Roles are collections of permissions.

items.label: Cloud KMS
items.note: Managed encryption keys, with the option to hold your own.

items.label: Secret Manager
items.note: Stores and versions credentials. Access is an IAM decision.

items.label: Identity-Aware Proxy
items.note: Puts a login in front of an app without changing the app.

items.label: Binary Authorization
items.note: Only lets signed, verified container images run in GKE.

items.label: Data Loss Prevention
items.note: Finds and masks sensitive data before it spreads.

panels.head: Data pipelines, AI and operations
panels.caption: Moving data around, putting a model on it, and the telemetry you will want the first time production misbehaves.

items.label: Pub/Sub
items.note: Global messaging. Publishers and subscribers never touch each other.

items.label: Dataflow
items.note: Runs streaming and batch pipelines. Managed Apache Beam.

items.label: Dataproc
items.note: Managed Spark and Hadoop clusters, billed by the second.

items.label: Cloud Composer
items.note: Scheduled workflow orchestration. Managed Apache Airflow.
Train and serve models, and reach Gemini through one API.

items.label: Cloud Build
items.note: Builds, tests and deploys from your repository.

items.label: Cloud Logging
items.note: Collects logs from every service in the project.

items.label: Cloud Monitoring
items.note: Metrics, dashboards and alerts. Formerly Stackdriver.

items.label: Cloud Audit Logs
items.note: Records who did what, where and when. The audit trail.
